business_problem: Stripe needed a CLI-native coding assistant that met enterprise security requirements and could be safely distributed to engineers without exposing corporate laptops to unapproved JavaScript packages or an unmanaged npm dependency chain.
solution_summary: Stripe's developer infrastructure team chose Claude Code for engineers who prefer a command-line workflow and worked with Anthropic over two to three months to produce a signed enterprise binary. The binary bypasses Claude Code's npm dependency chain, addressing concerns about supply-chain attacks from random JavaScript packages on corporate laptops. Stripe distributes it through its internal mechanism, pre-installed on laptops and development boxes and pre-configured with rules, tokens, and authentication, so engineers can use it without self-service accounts or setup. Engineers supply repository and documentation context; Claude Code understands the codebase, edits files, and runs commands while developers review and adapt outputs. The article reports a concrete Scala-to-Java migration using Claude models and describes training, all-hands, and team-level sharing to improve use. The story does not specify a separate data store or an automated deployment flow.

data_flow: Stripe engineers use pre-installed, pre-configured Claude Code with their codebase and internal documentation as context; Claude Code edits files and runs commands, and engineers review resulting changes. For a Scala-to-Java migration, Claude models converted 10,000 lines and enabled an upgrade to a newer JDK.
integration_points: Stripe developer laptops and development boxes
business_outcome: Stripe deployed Claude Code to 1,370 engineers through a zero-configuration enterprise rollout. One team migrated 10,000 lines of Scala to Java in four days, work estimated at ten engineering weeks by hand, enabling an upgrade to a newer JDK. Engineers reported higher satisfaction with their tooling, and Stripe is exploring agent-based incident detection and resolution.
